command: codex -a untrusted (interactive TUI, driven under a pty)
note: `-a untrusted` escalates anything outside codex's trusted set, so `rm` gates. The wiring is already right here — codex registers PermissionRequest — unlike claude-code, where the same capture found the event unregistered. Home path redacted to /Users/dev. Redacted: the `world_state` line, 29.7 KB of it, listed the maintainer's installed skills with their paths plus the host timezone. `world_state` is in codex's ignored set, so dropping it left the golden snapshot byte-identical — which is how the redaction was shown to cost no evidence. Sandbox: codex's own approval prompt was answered by the driver; the gate fires before the answer, so the capture holds it either way Redacted: the recorder's own MCP server / skill inventory (tool NAMES only, no credentials) to generic placeholders — a public repo and an immutable crates.io tarball are the wrong home for one machine's tooling roster, and no decoder reads those fields.
